reviews.text: 不推荐 无脑堆遗物游戏，妈的，跟那个游戏qq群的人说为什么不把遗物合成做了，他说不能抄的一模一样不是一个制作者，nm ui，游戏局外都一模一样了，他又给你说是克苏鲁卡牌制作的朋友。立体防御是吧。抄都不不会抄 ，把糟粕抄完了，游戏亮点不抄。问亮点为什么不抄就是不能抄袭。问局外为什么一样就是续作了，朋友了。 你们到底搞懂你们游戏的两点是什么了吗？？？ 不会是这卡牌池吗，你这个纯数值游戏！！
好玩很有潜力，卡牌构思不错喜欢杀戮尖塔的肯定会喜欢。 另外战斗攻击小国如果再明显点就好了
卡牌种类很多，整体流程非常爽。但是用一个强力的build就能打穿，所以卡牌种类多大多数没啥用。还是需要制作组平衡下卡牌效果。
只能说战斗爽，比另外一个同类型的克苏鲁游戏还要爽。 翻译有问题，比如一个扣血回理智的事件中，把血和理智搞反了，其他的还有一些，希望能尽快改过来。
爬塔肉鸽真挺上头的 而且卡牌设计很有想法，combo打起来特别流畅，画风也对我胃口
爬塔爬塔，放开我我要爬塔！这个战斗真的顶，而且肉鸽元素也有很高的标准，好玩爽完！

被群友偏进来玩的，尼玛好评都是刷的吧真离谱啊。评论还在什么流派、BD，把我整笑了。局外强化只要点出来三分一随便什么角色都是闭着眼睛乱杀，什么卡组构建，不存在的，纯粹的数值碾压。机器人是最离谱的，连牌都不用打，出门开战把自己技能点完就是30+的AOE伤害直接清场，拿点遗物和相关卡牌能直接打出90+，什么，卡牌游戏竟然还要打牌？ 理智值更是搞笑，我就第一把降到过1，后面局外强化点出来就没掉下过10，而且理智的消耗对游戏本身也几乎没有什么影响，既起不到血条的作用又不是个合格的资源。总结一下就是各方面的设计都凸显出一个无聊，通关之后几乎没有任何再玩的欲望。 更新一下回复吧，过于简单只是这个游戏最小的一个问题。简单当然可以在结果上导向“爽游”，但目前来看这个游戏显然导向的是“无聊”。 DBG卡牌游戏市面上真的很多，一个卡牌游戏在打牌方面需要些什么这里不赘述了，跟热门的几个一比就知道这游戏基本没沾边的，甚至可以说这直接导致了数值离谱的局外强化的产生。 抛开卡牌的数值和打牌的底层逻辑的设计不说。这游戏目前四个角色里三个有自己独特的机制，但是两个带宠的自身卡牌跟其独有机制几乎没有任何强关联。狗的战斗力就不说了，放狗的技能甚至不需要有狗，那狗存在的意义是什么？小机器人同理，唯一比狗强的地方就在于小机器人本身的行动比狗要强一点。剩下一个血怒哥，核心围绕血怒和卖血展开，“绝望”血越少伤害越高，但是由于难度过低，不刻意挨打我甚至不知道怎么掉血，这个两个机制直接废一半。所以这狗、小机器人、绝望的存在意义是什么？把这三个关键的机制删掉，对整个游戏的玩法来说会有明显的影响吗？ 再说理智值，作为克苏鲁游戏常见的第二血条，在这个游戏里当前的难度下完全起不到血条的作用，并且无论你的理智值是1还是30，都不会对角色的属性以及行为产生任何影响，都做克系游戏了老大哥暗黑地牢真就一点不学？而作为一种资源，既不需要规划其使用，也不能换到什么独特的、有重大收益的东西，显然也不是一个合格的资源。就现在的表现来看纯纯的硬套克苏鲁世界观整了个名为“理智值”的计数器出来，实际删掉这玩意对游戏0影响。 再来看关卡设计，第一关新手关没啥好说的，中间两张图难度没有任何区别，实际最后一关也只是局内游戏节奏不同，虽然部分敌人不一样，但是在目前这个难度下， whocare?包括boss在内都是路边一条，随便碾死。我不知道在开发者看来打中间那两张图的意义是什么？别跟我说是看这加起来不知道有没有两百字的剧情啊，那可真是把我逗笑了，我还专门刷了几遍前面的图，真是浪费时间。既然局外成长给这么离谱，那能不能学一下人家高殿战记或者穿越方尖碑，来点难度区分然后直接把这四张图串一起啊。 最后还是我比较疑惑的一点，这个游戏就算每个角色四张图全通一遍，流程大概在10小时左右，之后值得重复游玩点在哪里？
This game is a lot like 'Menace From the Deep' but on steroids - better. Best part? Meta-upgrades - Menace was lacking in this department.

Unfortunately pretty poorly balanced. Most encounters are either a complete joke and then a few that are completely unwinnable are sprinkled in. From what I saw, there doesn't seem to be much depth either. Almost all the cards I saw are just "Deal X damage" or "Gain X Block". Seems to be pretty grindy to unlock other characters too. Shame cause the visuals/setting seems pretty cool.

The core gameplay is solid but there is a serious lack of content. I got 100% completion within 9.5 hours. There is a very limited pool of enemies and events so most runs are very similar. Also, the balance is all over the place with most battles being mindlessly easy with an occasional sharp spike in difficulty. The first section of the fourth map is so much more difficult than the others it feels like a different game. Some characters (the mech) and mechanics (stun and spark) are so overpowered that it feels pointless to make any other build. With the mech, I won 95% of battles before the enemy could even take a turn. I enjoyed the aesthetic and the core of the gameplay but cannot recommend the game until there is a substantial increase in content and an overall balance pass.

So the start of this game was enjoyable. The first character unfortunately is probably the only one worth playing. When you unlock the rest and try them out they seem like the battles were not balanced for them at all and some of them can't even get done with a run without lots of grinding/investment. The game battles overall are either really easy to beat or impossible to do. Dots are overpowered and don't fall off over time. This breaks the game or makes fights impossible if you're on the receiving end and you die because you have 50 stacks of enemy poisons and can't shield yourself more than 7-14 damage a turn. There;s also a couple battles that you can start and die in 1 turn if you didn't draw enough block first turn to defend against the 150 incoming damage on you. This makes these fights unenjoyable as you often can't do anything about it. I'd advise waiting to buy until balance changes are made or until it goes on sale for like a $1.
came here from game Menace of the Deep, unfortunately I am dissapointed, whoever did the toxicity buff on enemies, should be ashamed

哈哈，这评论区都演哥们呢，这能90好评？我的评价是不如蠕行恐惧的东西（没有说你蠕行恐惧做的好的意思），一共四个战役初见3小时不到直接给你从头到尾打穿了。毫无策略性，这几把哪来的构筑可言？所有角色bd一眼望到头，随便点点局外更是超级碾压，打到后面都不用考虑拿什么牌了，路上拿到key牌直接一路跳过。bro战斗里面所有技能点一遍，牌全都划出去直接获胜。无脑爽也无脑的不够彻底，删牌手段过少，想给自己设限玩点花活都做不到，打到结束基础牌都丢不完一半，不上不下卡这了。这么爱爽不如拤管子倒腾两下，比这爽一百倍。 我的评价是孬。

None of that ended up mattering, because after a few days and four hours of gameplay, as well as multiple attempts to uninstall/reinstall it never actually started up again. Just locked before even getting to the main screen every time. That's some unprofessional ♥♥♥♥.
喜欢这种卡牌肉鸽类的游戏，感觉遗物和塔罗牌种类比较少，跟蠕行的恐惧比较像，希望能像蠕行似的几个遗物能组合成更强大的遗物就更好了

I picked this up after playing "Menace from the Deep" (it was recommended) and I was really pleased with the game. Addictive gameplay loop, cool cards and upgrades etc. I quite liked the variety of missions - gave me something to keep coming back to play. Characters were pretty decent if a little archetypal. I couldn't find fault with much of anything - except H.U.G.O. - H.U.G.O. is about as useful in battle as a marzipan sword.
Copies Menace from the Deep to such a degree that I was certain it's the same dev (it isn't). Though at the same time improves on almost every mechanic, so still highly recommend.

To be honest it was very boring and not engaging at all. I skipped all the story text because it was not interesting at all. So much grinding, repetition, and endless loops. The first 3 levels are doable, but the last 4th one is not doable at all, unless you are willing to repetitively grind for a whole bunch of days to try to level up your characters to try to take on the last 4th level. Regretting all the time wasted into this. Recommend investing your valuable time elsewhere.

Great deckbuilder, basically refined version of Menace of the deep.

Somewhere between Menace of the Deep's complexity and sometimes insane difficulty spikes, and this game's simplicity and boring, if easy, road to victory, there is probably a great game. This game is a dumbed down version of Menace w/ less story, easier progression, and it really doesn't take long to see just about everything the game has to offer. Which isn't much, even for a fan of Menace like I am. I would say pass or buy on deep discount, you'll finish almost all of it too quickly to really enjoy it.

Solid game. But not much unique stuff. A lot of mechanics were taken from "Menace from the Deep" and imroved. Also music and voice acting are quite good, but sometimes Ukrainian subtitles are wrong after boss fights

From what I read, just like the original Sovereign Syndicate game was heavily borrowing its gameplay elements from Disco Elysium, this one borrows heavily from Menace of the Deep. Having played neither of them as of writing this review, a sucker for anything steampunk and Victorian fantasy, who very much enjoyed the atmosphere and lore of the first Sovereign Syndicate game, for me this game was an instabuy. Very different genre from the original, but nonetheless very fun, if a little bit short and occasionally grindy for my taste.

Overall pretty nice but definitely need more content. Also the game is overall really easy for a game of this type. I've lost I think a total of 4 times. The balance is also all over the place, once you find something that works since there's not that much content it's very easy to only do that every run.

一款非常无聊的卡牌RPG。每个角色的牌的种类非常的少，都不到30张。游戏非常的肝但又肝的无趣，因为游戏难度极低，初见乱玩就能过关，通关后有局外成长，但敌人却没有任何变化，再加之游戏卡牌内容少，通关几次就根本不想再碰了

I think this game is okay overall. It isn't hard and the grind of going for 100% like in Menace of the deep is a lot shorter. It's fine for what it is but there are several pros and cons about this game that I should get into for anyone looking for a roguelite deckbuilder. Overall the artstyle is nice and the sound track isn't bad either. It's very stylized and that isn't a bad thing at all. Meta progression feels pretty good like it makes a massive difference in your power, but there are draw backs to that heavy power from progressing. Achievements to 100% this game are pretty straight forward and simple and just need some grind to get finished. The game feels very manageable after your first 1-2 runs making it so you steamroll through the content pretty easy. The negatives to this game however are kind of high. For one, the 4th act is a massive difficulty spike from the other 3 expecting you to have beaten the other 3 acts 7-8 times each at least if you want to take on the challenging final one. Another unfortunate thing is that the meta progression isn't cards or relics since you have access to every card and every relic right off the bat. There are no additional unlocks for any of the things you will find on the run which makes it kind of dull having a full run allow you to see almost every card and relic available to you making for very samey runs since you will probably get the same cards and the same relics to finish. Unlike other deck builders, this game feels like there is basically only 1 or at most 2 ways to play the agents which heavily limits any form of build variety. The mental health meter similar to Darkest Dungeon's stress bar hardly will ever be taken into account as if you've been given far too much to finish the run. On top of that, the system uses something called Doom where as you progress and pick different locations, the longer it takes to get to the end, the more scaling the enemies get which often wasn't a problem and easily avoided as long as you didn't make decisions like +1 energy per turn at the cost of faster doom scaling. Having maxed out characters often made this stat a nonfactor anyway and it was simple to keep in check. The overall balancing seems a little off where some runs seem extremely easy like you will melt the boss down to nothing before it even does anything if you know what you're doing. Most bosses even until now I don't even know if they were threatening because they just die in a few good turns. You get few chances to upgrade and removing cards is extremely easy so it's very possible to go into infinites with 0 cost draws on some characters. Enemy variety isn't really all there. 3-4 types of rats, 5-8 types of humans, 5-7 types of man-made machines, 7-9 types of creatures/beasts and a handful of bosses. Sounds like a lot but the issue is every fight usually contains 1-4 different kinds of these enemies so you end up seeing the entire chafe roster in a few runs minus some bosses. Different acts you'll even see the enemy types bleed across them so you'll know what you're fighting right away before the fight starts. It's nice that there are animations for the characters but the game can break if you play cards too quickly. Characters only attack for the first animation while the other hits go through like normal and they just stand there which was a little disappointing. However, something that was annoying was if you played your cards too fast, sometimes the game doesn't even register you played a card. It goes to discard, it gets played, it doesn't have any effects and you just wasted energy on nothing. Trying to rush through spam clicking has broken the game before and was a slight issue for me when trying to 100% Menace from the Deep. Overall this game is a dumbed down version of Menace from the Deep and if you want a power crept deck builder with little challenge, this one might be the one for you. For what it is despite having many negatives, this game is just considered fine. It's not great, it's not the worst thing in the world, it's just okay. Get it on a discount though because this game doesn't really have a lot to it.

I like that it feels like an adventure game, or a sort of linear "RPG", but with card-battler combat. You control one hero at a time, out of four, and each has totally unique abilities and perks. I really enjoyed the game. [b]The difficulty[/b] : It is challenging, but accessible. All in all, I failed 7 missions: 1 early mission from bad luck, and I died about 6 times doing the last and hardest location. I needed to grind/upgrade my characters a bit (there are four characters), but I still had a hard time. I completed the game 100% with all characters. The last location felt sometimes dangerous and tricky, and I had to be cautious against the bosses, but it is not too difficult: enough though that you do feel happy when you succeed. __ Note that trying to get [b]100% achievements[/b] is doable, but it takes at least an extra 10+ hours of grind. I got 100%, but I cannot say I enjoyed that grind. :P Of course, most sane people will not try to get 100% achievements. __ NB: and, yes, I have played games like Slay the Spire ; though I am not great at it. PS: If you like the concept of RPG/adventure meets card-battler combat, you might like [i]Deep Sky Derelict[/i]. It is really a scifi RPG and well done in my opinion (while Hunter's Moon is more of linear adventure).

差点以为是蠕行的恐惧一家做的，没想到独游还能抄来抄去的，我服了，强烈不推荐，抵制复刻式抄袭！！甚至在游玩过程中看到偷了隔壁素材的图标，忘记删了可还行，气笑了。 卡牌数值做的一点灵魂都没有，很多卡的强度也抽象，答辩金卡和神级铜卡一堆。表面上是卡牌游戏，实际上是数值砍怪游戏，个人觉得这家对卡牌游戏的理解可能停留在抄袭上了。 （玩的久是因为很早以前就在库里了，不玩浪费，时长是因为大部分时间都是挂后台排队时候玩的，所以虚高。 顺便安利下《蠕行的恐惧：克苏鲁选集》，这游戏照抄的对象，很好玩的卡牌游戏，很有自己的想法，我很喜欢。
What a great idea having the final boss's attack pattern be to stun you first and then follow up with 150 damage while you have no control of your character.
难度有些过于低了，很快索然无味，感觉不如它的姊妹游戏《蠕行的混沌：克苏鲁选集》。

Hunter’s Moon is a roguelite deckbuilder where the player must protect Victorian-era London from werewolves and other strange monsters. Combat will feel familiar to fans of other deckbuilders, while the progression of each run is very similar to Menace From The Deep. [h1]Combat[/h1] • At the start of each turn you’ll randomly draw a few cards from your deck, which allow you to attack, defend, or perform special abilities such as applying status effects to yourself or an enemy. Cards cost energy to play, and you have a limited amount of energy per turn. • Unused block reduces by half at the end of turn instead of disappearing completely. This means that even if you’re not being attacked on the current turn, playing a defence card isn’t a complete waste. However, this effect also applies to enemies. • The player character has both a health bar and a sanity meter. While most enemy attacks deal health damage, some monsters can reduce your sanity. You’ll die if either health or sanity reaches zero. Some cards or relics spend sanity points to apply buffs. • One of the biggest differences compared to MFTD is that your cards don’t earn XP when you play them, so you won’t be able to upgrade them as often. • You can acquire relics and tarot cards which provide passive bonuses that can synergise with your cards, however there are no MFTD style set bonuses. • There are four playable characters who each have their own unique cards which provides different playing styles. Molly has a pet dog who will attack enemies, and her defence cards can be used to protect the dog. Grizwald has a pet robot and focuses on electricity attacks. Jericho is a bit like Slay The Spire’s Watcher. He gains rage points from playing attack cards, which will eventually double damage dealt and received, so the order you play cards is really important. My favourite, Nandi, has powerful poison and defence cards, making her a combination of STS’s Silent and Ironclad. [h1]Story Mode[/h1] • Each run features four acts, and you’ll visit various locations, including normal and elite fights, random encounters where you’ll choose between different options and receive rewards or penalties, a museum where you can acquire a relic or upgrade a card, the tavern where you can restore health, a gypsy who will give you tarot cards, and the merchant where you can buy relics, cards, or consumables. And of course, each act ends with a boss fight. • Instead of the usual deckbuilder node layout, Hunter’s Moon uses MFTD’s travel deck system. Each location is a card which is shuffled into multiple decks in a random order. The player can pick the top card (which is shown face up so you know what it is) from either deck. This system provides a lot of tactical flexibility, allowing you to visit the merchant when you have plenty of money, or save a tavern for when you’re low on health. • Unlike MFTD, travel cards don’t cost fuel, which means there’s no instant game over for running out. Instead, each card increases a doom meter, which gradually makes enemies more powerful. • There’s also a meta progression layer where you’ll earn bonuses to make future runs easier. You need to gather scrap metal from certain locations in the travel deck to upgrade buildings in your base, and you’ll also earn XP from each run which lets you upgrade each character’s abilities. • A full run should take between 60 and 90 minutes to complete and it took me 12 hours to defeat the final boss and complete the story mode. There’s not really much to do after this other than try to unlock a few more achievements. • The story itself is quite basic, voice acting is poor, and the ending is anticlimactic. [h1]Recommendation[/h1] Hunter’s Moon is a fairly good deckbuilder which fans of the genre should enjoy. It doesn’t have the long term replayability of the most popular games, but its worth picking up on a sale to play through the story mode.
Very poor game. Very boring, and very amateurish. Expected a lot, lot better.

In the week since I’ve gotten Hunter’s Moon, I’ve put more than 30 hours into it. While it has a few fun twists on common rogue-like deckbuilder mechanics and a solid theme, I suspect it grabbed me because of how powerful the characters feel when they revisit old locations or find the right synergies. But initially, I had mixed feelings about the game, because the first few locations seemed too easy to provide a sense of accomplishment. I kept waiting for an optional way to ramp up the difficulty, but outside of a randomly-available tarot card that accelerates monster growth, I couldn't find one. This was worrying, because as the player gains experience, they also gain access to upgrades that make their decks even stronger. Eventually, I realized that the difficulty selection comes from deciding which of the four mission locations to visit. If I wanted to relax and feel powerful, or to gather materials to unlock permanent upgrades, I could send the armored scientist Grizwald back to the initial location and leverage the upgrades I’d already unlocked to zap the enemies into oblivion. When I wanted more of a challenge, I could dispatch my least favorite character to face the ultimate big bad. Revisiting the less challenging locations to relax still gave me the occasional sense of discovery by exposing me to sub-missions or single-choice encounters I hadn’t seen before. It was also fun to experiment with different deck compositions in a low-stakes environment. The game’s card pool feels small, but it’s augmented by three other ways to power up decks outside the permanent upgrades: relics, powerful objects that grant passive bonuses; tarot cards, which either offer minor upgrades or significant benefits at the cost of downsides; and consumables, which can only be used once but sometimes have powerful effects. Add in the ability to upgrade cards, which sometimes significantly changes their effects, and there’s plenty of synergies to explore. As much as I enjoyed Hunter’s Moon, I have a few minor quibbles with it. For example, the game has a status called Focus that says all aggressive actions must be directed at the character with it, yet the player can ignore it and attack other characters. The enemy seems to have the same freedom when one of the player characters gains Focus. I also found some of the card designs strange. It baffles me that a character who eventually gains the ability to regenerate every turn has cards that encourage her to be at low health or provide healing, but those cards at least have some use early on. Other cards, such as the attacks that bypass enemy defenses or the ones that encourage Grizwald to toggle between different passive abilities called modes, never felt like they justified their cost. On the bright side, the characters’ unlockable talents and the cards themselves do a good job of pointing the player in fruitful directions. For example, Nandi has one upgrade path related to protecting herself and another that focuses on weakening enemies, hinting that her decks can build an impenetrable defense or poison enemies and watch them gradually expire. Meanwhile, the reformed thief Molly has talents that focus on hitting hard and fast or give her loyal dog extra staying power. The story is solid as long as you’re looking for a pulpy steampunk setting rather than a character-driven tale or a deep mystery. Hunter’s Moon can be compelling, but if you have a tight budget and enough free time to need something that will consume hundreds of hours, I’d look at other roguelike deckbuilders, such as Monster Train 2, Chrono Ark or Slay the Spire. I doubt the final mission, the various strategies for each character, or the story encounters offer enough variety to push the game past 40 hours. If that isn’t a problem for you, I’d recommend Hunter’s Moon, especially if you like the steampunk aesthetic or want something where you’ll eventually feel quite powerful.

This is one of those that define good, but not great. It's like any number of deck building rogue lites that you've played before. So the backdrop of this one is you get 1 of 4 different characters that allow you to play as with 4 unique deck styles. Good. The story. I actually really like the way the story is presented. I think the quest system going through each of it's 4 maps is pretty neat (The last map is just the final boss run) I think they do a good job establishing the lore and give some contact to the things you're doing in the game. It's rare you get that a whole lot in the deck builders so I'm happy with it. Sound design. Both in terms of voice acting and music. I wouldn't call either great, but both are very solid for a base price game of $20. Art direction. I think they do a good job with the eldritch style both for the monsters, characters and the backgrounds. Bad. Class balance. The game really only seems to have 2 viable end game classes . with one other one being kind of mid, and one being just awful. This is pretty disappointing. Difficulty spikes. The games difficulty spikes feel more frustrating than fun. Especially going to the last fight where it seems grinding out levels and additional bonuses is the only way to win due to how little you get before the fight. Overall number of cards. The game really feels out of sorts with the different builds you can do within each class. It looks like the game really wants you to play one of two ways if you want to win which is disappointing. Overall grade: C+ For $20 it's solid pick up if you get it on sale like I did I think it's a very worthwhile buy. Just don't think it's going to reach the heights of a Slay the Spire, Inception, or even the Tainted Grail card game.
